title: Structure sections on a reduced scheme away from component intersections
statement: Let $X$ be a reduced scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$ be closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose underlying sets cover $X$. Put $T=\bigcup_{i\ne j}(Z_i\cap Z_j)$. Then $X\setminus T$ is the scheme-theoretic union of the open subschemes $Z_i\setminus T$, these opens are pairwise disjoint, and for every open $U\subseteq X\setminus T$ restriction is an isomorphism $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)\cong\prod_i\Gamma(U\cap Z_i,\mathcal O_{Z_i})$ (with empty factors omitted).

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NE, proof, first paragraph after setting T

proof.text: Write $X^\circ=X\setminus T$ and $W_i=(Z_i\cap X^\circ)_{\mathrm{top}}$. Each $Z_i\cap Z_j$ is closed in $X$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion], so their finite union $T$ is closed and $X^\circ$ is open. If a point of $X^\circ$ lay in both $W_i$ and $W_j$ with $i\ne j$, it would lie in $T$; hence the $W_i$ are pairwise disjoint. They cover $X^\circ$ because the $Z_i$ cover $X$ set theoretically. Each $W_i$ is closed in $X^\circ$, and its complement is the finite union of the other closed $W_j$; thus each $W_i$ is also open. This includes $r=0$ (then $X^\circ=\emptyset$) and $r=1$ (then $T=\emptyset$).

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NE (varieties-lemma-glue-invertible-sheaves), proof, first paragraph after setting T; finite closed-cover topology written out

proof.text: Give $W_i$ its open subscheme structure in $X^\circ$ [def-pc-scheme]. The restriction of the closed immersion $Z_i\hookrightarrow X$ to $W_i$ is a closed immersion with underlying image all of $W_i$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. On any affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq W_i$, it is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ for the ideal $I=\mathcal I_i(V)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and full support means $V(I)=\operatorname{Spec}R=V(0)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], $\sqrt I=\sqrt0$. Since $V$ is open in the reduced scheme $X$, $R$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme], so $\sqrt0=0$; hence $I=0$. Thus the restricted closed immersion is an isomorphism on every affine open $V$ and consequently $Z_i\setminus T\cong W_i$ as schemes over $X^\circ$. The $W_i$ are disjoint open subschemes covering $X^\circ$, so their scheme-theoretic union is $X^\circ$: on every affine open its defining ideal is locally the zero ideal, since one $W_i$ contains each point.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NE (varieties-lemma-glue-invertible-sheaves), proof, first paragraph: 'As X is reduced we have X minus T = union (Z_i minus T) as schemes'; affine ideal argument supplied

proof.text: For an open $U\subseteq X^\circ$, the finitely many $U_i=U\cap W_i$ are pairwise disjoint opens covering $U$ by step 1. The structure sheaf of the scheme [def-pc-scheme] satisfies the sheaf axiom, so a section on $U$ is uniquely a tuple of sections on the $U_i$: compatibility on $U_i\cap U_j=\emptyset$ is automatic, since a sheaf of rings has the unique section on the empty open. By step 2, $U_i\cong U\cap Z_i$ as open subschemes of $Z_i$; restriction therefore identifies $\mathcal O_X(U_i)$ with $\mathcal O_{Z_i}(U\cap Z_i)$. Combining these identifications gives the asserted restriction isomorphism, also when a factor is empty or when $U=\emptyset$.
